**Scope note:** this guards the JavaScript `process.stdout/stderr.write` wrappers, so it contains writes from plugins, the worker's server logging, and `--print-logs`.

It does **not** contain writes made by native code straight to the file descriptor — e.g. the ALSA diagnostics block in #41763 / #41770. Same class of bug, but that needs fd-level redirection (`dup2`), not a JS wrapper.

The same mechanism is what makes this safe: opentui writes frames natively, so frame output never passes through these wrappers. Verified — a guard installed *before* `createCliRenderer` captured zero frame bytes while rendering stayed correct.

The `Expand-Archive -Path` switch treats `[` and `]` as wildcard chars, and interpolating a path with apostrophes into a single-quoted PowerShell string breaks the quoting...... the two bugs compound. Easiest robust fix in `Archive.extractZip()`: pass paths as argv to `powershell.exe` and switch to `-LiteralPath` on both `-Path` and `-DestinationPath` (that disables wildcard globbing). Also worth a sanity pass over `extractTar` and friends...... same interpolation pattern usually shows up there too.

Same root cause, third symptom — confirmed on v1.18.9 (Linux x64).

**Symptom:** `failed to load plugin @dietrichgebert/ponytail error="path must be a string or a file descriptor"` at startup.

**Trace:** the ponytail module exports the plugin as `default` (a plain function, so `readV1Plugin(..., "detect")` misses it) plus a named helper `parseCommandFile(filePath)`. `getLegacyPlugins` calls *every* function export with the PluginInput object → `parseCommandFile(input)` → `fs.readFileSync(input)` → `TypeError: path must be a string or a file descriptor`. The entire plugin silently fails to load; the error gives zero hint that a non-plugin export is the culprit.

**Confirming evidence for this issue:** same "invoke every export" behavior, surfacing as a raw fs TypeError instead of the `undefined.config`/`undefined.provider` crashes. Repro is trivial — any legacy plugin module that also exports a named helper function that touches fs.

**Possible fix direction:** in `getLegacyPlugins`, only treat the `default` export (or exports matching an explicit plugin contract) as plugins and skip the rest, plus wrap invocations so the error names the offending export. A plugin author who exports utilities alongside the plugin is a legitimate pattern and shouldn't be a footgun.

Saw the 479-byte stub after your `npm install -g opencode-ai` reinstall...... classic Defender signature-match swallowing the binary copy in postinstall.mjs. The `fs.linkSync` / `copyFileSync` fallback in that script swallows the failure and exits 0, so npm thinks everything's fine. Easiest unblock: add opencode-ai's npm cache + your `%LOCALAPPDATA%\npm-cache\_npx` and the global install path to a Defender exclusion, then rerun `npm install -g opencode-ai`. Or just disable real-time protection for the install window and re-enable. Btw, I keep a portable Hermes-OTG on a USB stick for exactly these 'Windows toolchain half-broken' moments...... imo, runs the same agent framework side-by-side so you can keep working while the install heals. https://github.com/MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG

Two real bugs in one. The PowerShell-7-only `Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive` getting picked first is the autoloader doing exactly what the docs say it'll do...... it stops at the first compatible-looking match and never falls back to System32. Fix for that: strip the MSIX `$PSHOME\Modules` from `PSModulePath` before opencode spawns 5.1 (`Expand-Archive`'s real home), or just launch opencode from a non-MSIX shell. Bug 2 is rougher...... `Effect.cached` wrapping a failing effect is a 'never retry until restart' footgun, and that's basically the contract nobody wants from a tool resolver. Until that's patched, the workaround you posted (drop `rg.exe` into `~/.cache/opencode/bin` + restart) is what works. Oh also, btw, I built a portable Hermes OTG and I keep it on USB for the 'every Grep call retries the same broken download' days...... imo, side-by-side agent helps you keep diagnosing while the upstream fix lands. https://github.com/MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG

## Additional evidence since this was closed — Aug 17 burst

Closing as "not planned" makes sense for the list-deployment mismatch alone, but the regression has gotten **measurably worse** since Aug 15, and I have hard data that wasn't in the original report. Requesting re-evaluation.

### Context

- OpenCode **1.17.18** on Linux, `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` covering 88 days
- Subscriber of OpenCode Go, using `providerID=opencode-go`
- Network is healthy: `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models` returns 200 in 0.4–0.5s from my region

### Numbers (single user, 88 days)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total stream errors | **116** |
| Errors on `providerID=opencode-go` | **97 (84%)** |
| Burst day (2026-08-17, 24h) | **73 errors** |
| Models with at least 1 error | 7 of 26 |
| `Failed after 3 attempts` (silent retry exhaustion) | 6 |

### Timeline correlation with @opencode announcements

The bursts are not random — they line up with public changes:

| Date | Public change | Error signature in my log |
|---|---|---|
| **Aug 12** | "DeepSeek V4 Pro now available in OpenCode Go" | 5× `deepseek-v4-pro` — *"only available hosted in China and requires explicit opt in"* |
| **Aug 16** | "DeepSeek has officially increased their prices. OpenCode Go's limits have been updated to reflect them" | First `kimi-k2.6` errors appear, plus the cooldown pattern matching #42935 (quota vaporization) |
| **Aug 17** | "Operation Cheepseek: Phase 1 Complete — $30 of usage for $10. Phase 2 initiating..." | 52× `kimi-k2.6` + 16× `qwen3.6-plus` + 15× `qwen3.7-max` in 24h |

So the original #42962 bug is now actively being made worse by an in-flight migration.

### Per-model breakdown (sorted by error count)

| Model | Errors | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `kimi-k2.6` | 52 | 503 — `Endpoint is unavailable` |
| `qwen3.6-plus` | 16 | 503 — `Endpoint is unavailable` |
| `qwen3.7-max` | 15 | 503 — `Endpoint is unavailable` |
| `kimi-k3` | 6 | 503 — `Endpoint is unavailable` |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | 5 | 400 — China-only opt-in, listed for non-CN users |
| `qwen3.7-plus` | 2 | 503 |
| `qwen3.8-max` | 1 | 503 |

### Retry pattern (no backoff)

Same session, same model, 5–7 errors per minute, no exponential backoff observed:

```
ses_fefce60ebffe7rC1cmd6FsBNB2 → 20 retries
ses_fef7aa8d4ffe0TyZaWDxGtvDOz → 16 retries
ses_fefea7fe6ffeMUnnn081BCr9nq → 12 retries
```

Each retry counts against quota (otherwise users would not have hit #42935 quota exhaustion). This compounds the user cost of the upstream outage.

### Verbatim log evidence (representative)

```
timestamp=2026-08-17T14:17:20.629Z run=... message="stream error" providerID=opencode-go modelID=kimi-k2.6
  error.error="AI_APICallError: Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable."

timestamp=2026-08-17T14:48:11.615Z run=... message="stream error" providerID=opencode-go modelID=kimi-k2.6
  error.error="AI_APICallError: Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable."

timestamp=2026-08-17T20:58:42.315Z run=... message="stream error" providerID=opencode-go modelID=qwen3.6-plus
  error.error="AI_APICallError: Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable."

timestamp=2026-08-17T20:59:51.416Z run=... message="stream error" providerID=opencode-go modelID=qwen3.6-plus
  session.id=ses_fee79fc78ffeF9AseAY753QeF9 small=false agent=build mode=primary
```

### Why "not planned" doesn't hold

Closing the list-vs-deployment issue as "not planned" was reasonable when models were *occasionally* out of sync. But:
1. The Phase 1 of Operation Cheepseek creates a **new normal** of frequent upstream migrations
2. Each migration leaves 3–6 stale entries in the catalog without surfacing availability
3. Users have no signal and no workaround other than reading your Twitter manually
4. Combined with the no-backoff retry (#43060, also closed as not planned), outages have a multiplicative cost

Very often I can already tell the plan is viable halfway through the response, but I still have to wait for the entire plan to finish generating before I can act on it. If the agent could proactively ask "Ready to switch to Build mode?" mid-generation, that would save a significant amount of tokens.

Even without proactive asking, a dedicated shortcut key to approve the plan would be a huge improvement. Right now the workflow is: manually switch to Build mode → type "go" / "yes" / "execute" — which feels unnecessarily clumsy.

Plan mode is essentially generating a TODO list. What if there was a clear, explicit UI action (like a button or shortcut) to approve the plan and start executing the TODOs, instead of having to express approval in natural language every time?

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.
